name: Neutral
character: Pure greyscale with a near-black accent, so nothing on the page competes with the content.
use: Documentation, dashboards and sites where the interface should stay in the background.
upstreamDescription: Quiet, warm greys that keep the focus on the content.

name: Butter
character: Cream paper with one bright blue accent.
use: Marketing pages and product launches with one strong colour.
upstreamDescription: Creamy yellows with a friendly blue accent, playful for consumer products and still easy to read.

name: Chocolate
character: Warm browns, with serif headings over a sans-serif body.
use: Editorial sites, long reads and pages with a printed feel.
upstreamDescription: Rich browns with Fraunces headings, an Albert Sans body and Lucide icons.

name: Matcha
character: Deep green on paper, with headings in a handwriting font and soft, rounded corners.
use: Craft, food and wellbeing sites that should feel handmade.
upstreamDescription: Calm, earthy greens with a natural feel, for wellness and content-first apps.

name: Stone
character: Cool grey with Montserrat headings over a Figtree body, quiet and formal.
use: Corporate and professional-services sites that want a restrained look.
upstreamDescription: Understated stone and slate colours with a slightly handmade feel.

name: Gothic
character: Near-white text on near-black, and the only theme that stays dark in light mode too.
use: Developer tools, music and products used mostly at night.
upstreamDescription: Deep blue-greys and a display serif, dramatic and editorial.

name: Y2K
character: Lavender background and square corners with no rounding at all.
use: Playful brands with a retro look and hard edges.
upstreamDescription: Hot pink, lime green and the Poppins font, playful and clearly retro.
